name: Straw Man
shortDef: Distorting someone's position into a weaker one, then attacking that.
definition: Restating someone's argument in an exaggerated, oversimplified or extreme form, then refuting that distorted version as if it were what they actually said.
howToSpot: Compare what was actually said with the version being attacked
Look for dropped qualifiers: 'some' becomes 'all', 'less' becomes 'none'
Ask whether the original speaker would accept this summary of their view
classicExample: Jen wants to cut the snack budget by 10%. So she wants everyone starving at their desks?
legitimateVersion: Summarizing someone's view and showing where it leads is fair when the summary is accurate and they'd recognize it, ideally checked with them or quoted in their own words.

contrast.fal_red_herring: A straw man distorts the opponent's actual position; a red herring drops the topic and brings in a different one.
contrast.fal_false_dichotomy: A straw man misrepresents one side's view; a false dichotomy pretends there are only two options to choose from.
